header.running_head: Severing Ties with the Period of Ignorance to Strengthen Ties with Islaam

blocks.text: Umar (RA) once passed by Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Al Aas (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "It seems to me that you are upset with me because you think that I had killed your father. Had I killed him, I would not have made any excuses for it because I killed my own maternal uncle Aas bin Hishaam bin Mughiera. Nevertheless, the truth is that when I passed by your father (on the battlefield) he was (lying down wounded and) hitting his head on the ground as a bull hits its horns on the ground. I then steered away from him and it was his cousin Ali who headed for him and killed him.[^1] Another narration adds that Hadhrat Sa'eed (RA) said, "Even if you killed him, it was you who was on the truth while he was on falsehood." This statement greatly pleased Hadhrat Umar (RA).[^2]
Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfah (RA)'s reaction when he Saw his Father's Body being Dragged to the Well After the Battle of Badr

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that according to the instructions of Rasulullaah ﷺ, the bodies of the Mushrikeen killed during the Battle of Badr were dragged to a (unused) well and thrown into it. Rasulullaah ﷺ then stood beside the well and said, "O people of this well! Have you found the promise of your Rabb (punishment) to be true? I have indeed found the promise of my Rabb (victory) to be true." The Sahabah (RA) asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Are you addressing dead people?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "They now know well that the promise of their Rabb is true."
Rasulullaah ﷺ noticed an expression of gloom on the face of Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfah (RA) as he saw the body of his father Utba being dragged to the well. "O Abu Hudhayfah!" Rasulullaah ﷺ called out, "It seems that you dislike what you are seeing?" Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfah (RA) replied, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Because my father was a leader of his people, I hoped that his Rabb would guide him to Islaam. However, it depressed me to see how he has fallen (without becoming a Muslim)." Rasulullaah ﷺ then made good du'aas for Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfah (RA).[^3]

Another narration from Hadhrat Abu Zinaad states that when Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfah (RA) fought in the Battle of Badr, he called his father Utba to challenge him to a duel. This narration also quotes the couplets that his sister Hind bin Utba (RA) recited about the incident.[^4]
